pr.title: Retry the Codex marketplace once when its clone fails
pr.head: d876ba8475aba0414416a7a1f555bd0e7a35e975

summary: install.sh installs Projector's CLI and its plugins for Claude Code and Codex, and project upgrade runs it to upgrade an existing install. The installer stops at the first host command that fails.

Codex keeps a Git marketplace as a clone, and it gives that clone a 30-second time limit of its own. On a slow connection, codex plugin marketplace upgrade projector can fail with git clone marketplace source timed out after 30s, and the whole upgrade fails with it. Running the upgrade again usually works.

This pull request makes the installer try again by itself. The two Codex commands that clone a marketplace, marketplace add and marketplace upgrade, now go through a wrapper. When the command fails, the wrapper prints a retrying row, waits five seconds, and runs the command once more. If the second try fails too, the installer stops with Codex's exit status, as it did before after the first failure.

groups.title: The installer retries a failed Codex marketplace command once
groups.kicker: A new wrapper in install.sh, used at the three call sites that clone
intro: run_codex runs a Codex command with the installer's Codex home directory. The new run_codex_with_retry runs it the same way, and on a failure runs it a second time after a five-second pause.

The installer runs under set -euo pipefail, so a failed command stops the script. The first try sits behind ||, which keeps its failure from stopping the script. The second try's status becomes the wrapper's return value, so a second failure stops the installer with Codex's own exit status.

files.note: Adds run_codex_with_retry and calls it from install_codex for both marketplace add branches and the Git marketplace upgrade branch.

checks.text: A second failure stops the installer with Codex's status. The test whose fake Codex fails every time sees the installer exit 3, the fake's status, and run no plugin add. A manual run with a fake Codex that exits 1 ended with exit 1.

Only the three marketplace commands that can clone are wrapped. marketplace remove and both plugin add calls still use run_codex, and a test confirms a failed Claude Code marketplace update runs once.

When a checkout has no origin remote, plugin_source returns the checkout's own path, so this add reads a local directory and clones nothing. A failure here still waits five seconds and blames a Git clone timeout. The review lists this as a suggestion rather than a finding, because the retry does no harm.

groups.title: Fake hosts that fail once, and a fake sleep
groups.kicker: Five installer tests for the retry, on fakes that can fail only the first time
intro: The installer tests put fake claude and codex commands on PATH, and a test makes a fake fail a command by writing it to a state file. A command written to the new <host>-fails-once file fails only the first time. Both kinds of failure now exit 3, a status the installer never uses, so a test can tell Codex's status from the installer's.
A fake sleep logs the pause instead of taking it, so the tests run without waiting.

files.note: Four tests cover the Codex upgrade: it works on the first try, works on the second, or fails twice, and Claude Code is not retried. A fifth, in ReleaseInstallTests, retries a failed marketplace add from a piped install.

checks.text: Against install.sh from main, the tests at lines 513, 532 and 840 fail, and at this head all 48 installer tests pass. The full suite, 927 tests with 1 skipped, passes too.
The installer never exits 3 itself: every literal exit and return in install.sh uses 0, 1, 64 or 69.
ReleaseInstallTests reuses InstallTests.setUp, so this piped test gets the fake sleep too and never pauses.

groups.title: The plugin guide describes the retry
groups.kicker: One sentence in the paragraph on upgrades
intro: The paragraph on how the installer upgrades what it installed gains one sentence. It names the two retried commands, the five-second pause, the retrying row, and the exit status after a second failure.

files.note: The new sentence matches run_codex_with_retry. The rest of the paragraph is rewrapped, not changed.
